newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended sharply up on the day after rallying along with German Bunds.
The March Confederate bond futures contract got as high as 116.68 during the day, breaking above the previous contract high of 116.37 set on December 20.
Bunds were supported by near-term expectations for weakness in the German economy.
Financial markets were waiting for release on Tuesday of U.S. consumer price index data (CPI) and retail sales.
Denmark launched a 200 million Swiss franc bond via Merrill Lynch with a repayment feature tied to currency fluctuations.

The bond repays at a minimum of 100.00. But if the mark, sterling or dollar outperform the Swiss franc, the premium at which it would be redeemed would be the same as the premium of the best-performing currency.

The bond, with a 2-1/4 percent coupon priced at 101.75 percent, aims to curb risk to investors, whether based in Swiss francs or other currencies, which may arise especially in view of uncertainties tied to plans for a European single currency.
"We are very pleased with the demand, we have seen strong demand from institutional investors private banks and others," one syndicate manager said.
Volume in the overall market was somewhat subdued. "Volume has not matched the huge price gains," one trader said, noting investors remained cautious given already low domestic yields.
The Swiss National Bank, meanwhile, appeared to be willing to continue its policy of fairly expansive monetary policy.
SNB board member Bruno Gehrig said in a newspaper interview that Switzerland's inflation risk is currently low.

Asked about prospects for further easing by the SNB, he said one should "never say never" but he also said that an excessively expansive monetary policy could lead to problems two or three years down the road.
Mar Comi medium-term bond up 19 at 111.29
Mar Euro Swiss francs up nine at 98.23.
